correctness.rationale: With Haar probability and ordinary trace characters, Schur orthogonality gives N=|a|²+|b|²+|c|² exactly. I reconstructed the Gram of (χ_V²,χ_V*²,χ_W²,χ_Vχ_V*,χ_Vχ_W,χ_V*χ_W) by Weyl integration: multiply each torus Laurent polynomial by the signed Vandermonde determinant, then take their coefficient dot products in the determinant-one exponent quotient, divided by 24. The diagonal is (2,2,3,2,2,2) and the only nonzero off-diagonal pairs have value 1 between the first two squares and 2 between χ_W² and χ_Vχ_V*. With the factors 2 in mixed expansion terms, this gives precisely the frozen M, including coefficients 2 and 8 in the two phase real parts. Writing x=|a|, y=|b|, z=|c|, S=x²+y² and p=xy, phase alignment gives the upper envelope 2S²+6p²+3z⁴+8z²(S+p). Its increase to p=S/2 is accounted for exactly by (3/2)(x²−y²)²+4z²(x−y)². The final envelope is (51/11)N²−(11/2)(z²−5N/11)². Restoring the two exact phase losses recovers all deficit terms. Equality at N>0 fixes x²=y²=3N/11, z²=5N/11, b/a=±1 and c²/(ab)>0, giving exactly the four projective classes. Each class saturates all losses; the zero function is trivial.
residual_risks: The finite Weyl calculation determines the exact polynomial, not its optimization by itself. No conclusion for dimension-normalized characters or arbitrary matrix coefficients.

The mixed character ratio exceeds that of any pure character and the established two-character subspace, with the sharp deficit pinpointing exactly which fusion couplings enforce a 3:3:5 energy split and four phase classes.
